claim: Slc1a5 is highly expressed in both naive calvarial cells and bone marrow stromal cells.
source: Slc1a5 is highly expressed in both naive calvarial cells and bone marrow stromal cells and significantly increases during osteoblast differentiation (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A comparing gene expression in growth media versus osteogenic media.

claim: Slc1a5 expression significantly increases during osteoblast differentiation.
source: Slc1a5 is highly expressed in both naive calvarial cells and bone marrow stromal cells and significantly increases during osteoblast differentiation (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A demonstrating increased Slc1a5 expression in osteogenic media compared to growth media.

claim: Slc1a5 targeting did not affect early osteoblast differentiation.
source: Slc1a5 targeting did not affect early osteoblast differentiation but did prevent the induction of the mature osteoblast genes Ibsp and Bglap and prevented matrix mineralization in primary calvarial cells (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR and functional assay data shown in Figure 1B-C comparing sgLuc control to sgSlc1a5 treated cells.

claim: Slc1a5 targeting prevented the induction of the mature osteoblast genes Ibsp and Bglap.
source: Slc1a5 targeting did not affect early osteoblast differentiation but did prevent the induction of the mature osteoblast genes Ibsp and Bglap and prevented matrix mineralization in primary calvarial cells (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B demonstrating reduced Ibsp and Bglap expression in sgSlc1a5 cells.

claim: Slc1a5 targeting prevented matrix mineralization in primary calvarial cells.
source: Slc1a5 targeting did not affect early osteoblast differentiation but did prevent the induction of the mature osteoblast genes Ibsp and Bglap and prevented matrix mineralization in primary calvarial cells (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by functional assays shown in Figure 1C demonstrating reduced alizarin red staining in sgSlc1a5 cells.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice were characterized by delayed endochondral and intramembranous ossification evident at both embryonic day E14.5 and E15.5.
source: Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice were characterized by delayed endochondral and intramembranous ossification evident at both embryonic (E) day E14.5 and E15.5 (Figure 1D–E–).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparation images shown in Figure 1D-E demonstrating reduced mineralization in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had reduced size of various skeletal elements relative to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ littermate controls.
source: In addition to delayed mineralization, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had reduced size of various skeletal elements (exemplified by the humerus, Figure 1F and J) relative to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ littermate controls (Figure 1F–G and J–K and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E-L).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparation measurements shown in Figure 1F-G and J-K demonstrating reduced humerus length.

claim: By E16.5 the extent of mineralization was no longer significantly different although the overall length of individual skeletal elements was significantly different from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ littermate controls.
source: By E16.5 the extent of mineralization was no longer significantly different although the overall length of individual skeletal elements was significantly different from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ littermate controls (Figure 1L–O and Figure 1—figure supplement 1M-P).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparation data shown in Figure 1L-O demonstrating recovery of mineralization but persistent length differences.

claim: At birth, neither matrix mineralization nor element length were significantly different suggesting there is a transient delay in endochondral ossification.
source: At birth, neither matrix mineralization or nor element length were significantly different suggesting there is a transient delay in endochondral ossification (Figure 1—figure supplement 1Q-X).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1Q-X demonstrating normalization of mineralization and length by birth.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice are characterized by impaired intramembranous ossification at all stages evaluated.
source: Conversely, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice are characterized by impaired intramembranous ossification at all stages evaluated (Figure 1D–E–, L–M and P–Q and Figure 1—figure supplement 1Q-R).
evidence: The claim is supported by skeletal preparation images shown in Figure 1D-E, L-M, P-Q demonstrating persistent calvarial defects.

claim: At birth, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae had increased porosity (1.0 ± 0.2 vs 2.3 ± 0.2 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05).
source: At birth, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae had increased porosity (1.0 ± 0.2 vs 2.3 ± 0.2 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05), increased suture width (1.0 ± 0.2 mm vs 1.4 ± 0.3 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) and significantly less bone volume (0.7% ± 0.02% vs 0.6 ± 0.05% in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) as measured by micro-computed tomography (µCT) (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by µCT measurements shown in Figure 1 demonstrating quantitative differences in calvarial bone parameters.

claim: At birth, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae had increased suture width (1.0 ± 0.2 mm vs 1.4 ± 0.3 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05).
source: At birth, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae had increased porosity (1.0 ± 0.2 vs 2.3 ± 0.2 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05), increased suture width (1.0 ± 0.2 mm vs 1.4 ± 0.3 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) and significantly less bone volume (0.7% ± 0.02% vs 0.6 ± 0.05% in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) as measured by micro-computed tomography (µCT) (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by µCT measurements shown in Figure 1 demonstrating quantitative differences in suture width.

claim: At birth, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae had significantly less bone volume (0.7% ± 0.02% vs 0.6 ± 0.05% in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05).
source: At birth, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae had increased porosity (1.0 ± 0.2 vs 2.3 ± 0.2 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05), increased suture width (1.0 ± 0.2 mm vs 1.4 ± 0.3 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) and significantly less bone volume (0.7% ± 0.02% vs 0.6 ± 0.05% in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) as measured by micro-computed tomography (µCT) (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by µCT measurements shown in Figure 1 demonstrating quantitative differences in bone volume.

claim: At 2-months of age, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice presented with less bone mass, increased suture width and altered suture morphology.
source: At 2-months of age, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice presented with less bone mass, increased suture width and altered suture morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by X-ray, µCT, and histological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Von Kossa staining of histological sections confirmed the reduction in mineralized bone matrix in newborn Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae.
source: Von Kossa staining of histological sections confirmed the reduction in mineralized bone matrix in newborn Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae (Figure 1T–U).
evidence: The claim is supported by von Kossa staining shown in Figure 1T-U demonstrating reduced mineralization.

claim: Slc1a5 expression in osteoprogenitors is essential for bone development.
source: Thus, Slc1a5 expression in osteoprogenitors is essential for bone development.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the cumulative data showing bone defects in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice.

claim: There was delayed mineralization in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae at E15.5.
source: Von Kossa staining confirmed there was delayed mineralization in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae at E15.5 (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by von Kossa staining shown in Figure 2A-D demonstrating reduced mineralization.

claim: There was no significant difference in the number of Sp7GFP expressing osteoblast progenitors per bone area in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice compared to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ wild type littermates (75.3% ± 11.6% vs 64.7±9.5 %).
source: This was not due to changes in the number of osteoblast progenitors as we observed no significant difference in the number of Sp7GFP expressing osteoblast progenitors per bone area in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice compared to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ wild type littermates (75.3% ± 11.6% vs 64.7±9.5 % in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ and Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/f animals, respectively) (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescent quantification shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: There was a significant reduction in the proportion of Sp7GFP cells that were positive for proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) (25.9% ± 4.6% vs 15.6±2.9 % in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ or Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05).
source: However, we did observe a significant reduction in the proportion of Sp7GFP cells that were positive for proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) (25.9% ± 4.6% vs 15.6±2.9 % in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ or Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) (Figure 2G–J) suggesting Slc1a5 is required for proliferation of Sp7 expressing osteoblast progenitors.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescent quantification shown in Figure 2G-J.

claim: Slc1a5 is required for proliferation of Sp7 expressing osteoblast progenitors.
source: However, we did observe a significant reduction in the proportion of Sp7GFP cells that were positive for proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) (25.9% ± 4.6% vs 15.6±2.9 % in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ or Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl respectively, p < 0.05) (Figure 2G–J) suggesting Slc1a5 is required for proliferation of Sp7 expressing osteoblast progenitors.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the reduced PCNA staining in Sp7GFP cells shown in Figure 2G-J.

claim: There were no significant differences in the expression of early osteoblast genes including alkaline phosphatase (Alpl) or Col1a1.
source: We did not observe significant differences in the expression of early osteoblast genes including alkaline phosphatase (Alpl, as determined by in situ staining) or Col1a1 (Figure 2K–N).
evidence: The claim is supported by alkaline phosphatase staining and in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2K-N.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl animals had reduced expression of the osteoblast differentiation genes Spp1 and Ibsp at both E15.5 and postnatal day 0 (P0).
source: Conversely, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl animals had reduced expression of the osteoblast differentiation genes Spp1 and Ibsp at both E15.5 and postnatal (P) day 0 (P0) (Figure 2O–T and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2O-T and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: The mature osteoblast gene Bglap was highly reduced at P0 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl compared to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ littermates.
source: Similarly, the mature osteoblast gene Bglap was highly reduced at P0 in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl compared to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ littermates (Figure 2U–V).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization shown in Figure 2U-V.

claim: Primary calvarial cells isolated from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice incorporated less EdU.
source: Consistent with these observations, primary calvarial cells isolated from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice incorporated less EdU and were characterized by reduced osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization in vitro (Figure 2W–X).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU incorporation assay shown in Figure 2X.

claim: Primary calvarial cells isolated from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice were characterized by reduced osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization in vitro.
source: Consistent with these observations, primary calvarial cells isolated from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice incorporated less EdU and were characterized by reduced osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization in vitro (Figure 2W–X).
evidence: The claim is supported by functional assays shown in Figure 2W.

claim: Acute SLC1A5 inhibition using GPNA reduced calvarial cell proliferation in vitro.
source: This is likely a direct effect of loss of Slc1a5 activity as acute SLC1A5 inhibition using GPNA reduced calvarial cell proliferation in vitro (Figure 2—figure supplement 1W).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1W demonstrating reduced proliferation with GPNA treatment.

claim: 2-month-old Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had reduced osteoblast numbers (exemplified by OCN expression).
source: Similarly, 2-month-old Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had reduced osteoblast numbers (exemplified by OCN expression) and significantly less trabecular bone volume as measured by µCT in the distal femur compared to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ wild-type littermate controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2J-N).
evidence: The claim is supported by OCN immunofluorescent staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2L-N.

claim: 2-month-old Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had significantly less trabecular bone volume as measured by µCT in the distal femur compared to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ wild-type littermate controls.
source: Similarly, 2-month-old Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had reduced osteoblast numbers (exemplified by OCN expression) and significantly less trabecular bone volume as measured by µCT in the distal femur compared to Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/+ wild-type littermate controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2J-N).
evidence: The claim is supported by µCT measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2J-K.

claim: Slc1a5 acts cell-autonomously to regulate osteoprogenitor proliferation and osteoblast differentiation.
source: Collectively, these data indicate Slc1a5 acts cell-autonomously to regulate osteoprogenitor proliferation and osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the cumulative data showing proliferation and differentiation defects in Slc1a5-deficient cells.

claim: Slc1a5 targeting significantly reduced 3H-proline incorporation into both collagen and total protein.
source: Slc1a5 targeting significantly reduced 3H-proline incorporation into both collagen and total protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: The claim is supported by radiolabeled proline incorporation assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Primary calvarial cells isolated from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had significantly reduced protein and collagen synthesis rates in vitro.
source: Likewise, primary calvarial cells isolated from Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had significantly reduced protein and collagen synthesis rates in vitro (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by radiolabeled proline incorporation assays shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: Slc1a5 is required for robust protein synthesis in osteoblasts.
source: These results indicate Slc1a5 is required for robust protein synthesis in osteoblasts.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the reduced protein synthesis rates in Slc1a5-deficient cells.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice were characterized by significantly less COL1A1 in both the calvariae and long bones at e15.5 and P0.
source: Consistent with the in vitro data, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice were characterized by significantly less COL1A1 in both the calvariae and long bones at e15.5 and P0 (Figure 3C–H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1Q-R and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescent staining shown in Figure 3C-H and supplemental figures.

claim: Col1a1 mRNA expression was not affected in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice.
source: It is important to note, Col1a1 mRNA expression was not affected in these mice indicating Slc1a5 provides amino acids required for robust COL1A1 synthesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2M-N showing no difference in Col1a1 mRNA.

claim: Slc1a5 provides amino acids required for robust COL1A1 synthesis.
source: It is important to note, Col1a1 mRNA expression was not affected in these mice indicating Slc1a5 provides amino acids required for robust COL1A1 synthesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Col1a1 mRNA is unchanged but COL1A1 protein is reduced.

claim: Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had a significant reduction in OSX protein expression.
source: Similarly, Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl mice had a significant reduction in OSX protein expression as we observed a reduction in the proportion of OSX expressing cells despite no change in Sp7GFP expression (used as a proxy for Sp7) in Sp7Cre;Slc1a5fl/fl calvariae (Figure 3I–N).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescent staining shown in Figure 3I-N.

claim: Slc1a5 is essential for the synthesis of proteins like OSX to regulate terminal osteoblast differentiation and COL1A1 necessary for bone matrix production.
source: Thus, Slc1a5 is essential for the synthesis of proteins like OSX to regulate terminal osteoblast differentiation and COL1A1 necessary for bone matrix production.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the reduced OSX and COL1A1 protein levels in Slc1a5-deficient mice.

claim: Slc1a5 targeting significantly diminished the intracellular abundance of many amino acids including reported substrates of SLC1A5 (e.g. asparagine, glutamine, and alanine) as well as amino acids not known to be transported by SLC1A5 (e.g. glutamate, lysine, histidine, aspartate, glycine, and proline).
source: Slc1a5 targeting significantly diminished the intracellular abundance of many amino acids including reported substrates of SLC1A5 (e.g. asparagine, glutamine, and alanine) as well as amino acids not known to be transported by SLC1A5 (e.g. glutamate, lysine, histidine, aspartate, glycine, and proline) (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Slc1a5 deletion also reduced the abundance of select TCA cycle intermediates including fumarate, malate, citrate, and a-ketoglutarate.
source: Moreover, Slc1a5 deletion also reduced the abundance of select TCA cycle intermediates including fumarate, malate, citrate, and a-ketoglutarate (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Only glutamine and to a lesser extent asparagine uptake was diminished in Slc1a5 targeted calvarial cells.
source: Interestingly, the uptake of many of these amino acids was unaffected in Slc1a5-deficient cells as only glutamine and to a lesser extent asparagine uptake was diminished in Slc1a5 targeted calvarial cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by radiolabeled amino acid uptake assays shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was a compensatory increase in the uptake of lysine in Slc1a5-deficient calvarial cells.
source: Conversely, we observed a compensatory increase in the uptake of lysine in Slc1a5-deficient calvarial cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by radiolabeled lysine uptake assays shown in Figure 4B.

claim: SLC1A5 transports glutamine and asparagine in osteoblasts.
source: Similar results were obtained upon acute SLC1A5 inhibition indicating SLC1A5 transports glutamine and asparagine in osteoblasts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GPNA treatment experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Slc1a5 inhibition significantly increased EIF2a Ser51 phosphorylation, a marker of amino acid depletion.
source: Slc1a5-deficient cells had many cellular changes consistent with decreased amino acid concentrations. For example, Slc1a5 inhibition significantly increased EIF2a Ser51 phosphorylation, a marker of amino acid depletion (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: There was a significant reduction in mTORC1 activity, as both ribosomal protein S6 Ser240/244 phosphorylation and Eif4ebp1 Ser65 phosphorylation were significantly reduced in Slc1a5-deficient calvarial cells.
source: Additionally, we observed a significant reduction in mTORC1 activity, as both ribosomal protein S6 Ser240/244 phosphorylation and Eif4ebp1 Ser65 phosphorylation were significantly reduced in Slc1a5-deficient calvarial cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: mTOR activation was not affected by acute SLC1A5 inhibition indicating decreased mTORC1 signaling may be a secondary effect of Slc1a5 deletion.
source: Interestingly, mTOR activation was not affected by acute SLC1A5 inhibition indicating decreased mTORC1 signaling may be a secondary effect of Slc1a5 deletion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that acute inhibition does not affect mTOR but genetic deletion does.

claim: SLC1A5 provides glutamine and asparagine to regulate intracellular amino acid homeostasis in osteoblast progenitors.
source: Collectively, these data indicate SLC1A5 provides glutamine and asparagine to regulate intracellular amino acid homeostasis in osteoblast progenitors.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the cumulative data showing reduced amino acid levels and altered signaling in Slc1a5-deficient cells.

claim: Depletion of either glutamine or asparagine from the media inhibited the induction of terminal osteoblast genes Ibsp and Bglap and prevented matrix mineralization.
source: Depletion of either glutamine or asparagine from the media similarly inhibited the induction of terminal osteoblast genes Ibsp and Bglap and prevented matrix mineralization (Figures 1B–C ,–5A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by functional assays and qRT-PCR shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Glutamine withdrawal had a more profound effect on osteoblast differentiation compared to either asparagine depletion or Slc1a5 ablation.
source: While this was reminiscent of Slc1a5 ablation, it is important to note that glutamine withdrawal had a more profound effect on osteoblast differentiation compared to either asparagine depletion or Slc1a5 ablation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing the effects of glutamine withdrawal, asparagine depletion, and Slc1a5 ablation on differentiation markers.

claim: Depletion of glutamine, but not asparagine, mimicked the effects of Slc1a5 targeting on both EIF2a Ser51 phosphorylation and mTORc1 activity.
source: Depletion of glutamine, but not asparagine, mimicked the effects of Slc1a5 targeting on both EIF2a Ser51 phosphorylation and mTORc1 activity (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Cells cultured in the absence of glutamine had reduced COL1A1 expression and decreased proliferation like Slc1a5 deficient cells.
source: Consistent with this, cells cultured in the absence of glutamine had reduced COL1A1 expression and decreased proliferation like Slc1a5 deficient cells (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot and EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: Culturing cells in the absence of asparagine had no discernable effect on either pSer51 Eif2a, pSer240/244 S6rp, or COL1A1 expression and enhanced proliferation as determined by increased EdU incorporation.
source: On the other hand, culturing cells in the absence of asparagine had no discernable effect on either pSer51 Eif2a, pSer240/244 S6rp, or COL1A1 expression and enhanced proliferation as determined by increased EdU incorporation (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot and EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: Culturing cells in the absence of either glutamine or asparagine had no effect on cell viability.
source: Importantly, culturing cells in the absence of either glutamine or asparagine had no effect on cell viability (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Annexin V staining shown in Figure 5E.

claim: SLC1A5 primarily provides glutamine to regulate amino acid homeostasis necessary for proliferation and osteoblast differentiation.
source: From these data, we conclude SLC1A5 primarily provides glutamine to regulate amino acid homeostasis necessary for proliferation and osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the differential effects of glutamine versus asparagine withdrawal.

claim: SLC1A5 provides asparagine which is essential for terminal osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization.
source: Additionally, SLC1A5 provides asparagine which is essential for terminal osteoblast differentiation and matrix mineralization.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the effects of asparagine depletion on differentiation markers and mineralization.

claim: Glutamine carbon contributes to all TCA cycle intermediates and was significantly enriched in several amino acids (e.g. glutamate, aspartate, alanine, and proline) found to be reduced in Slc1a5 targeted cells.
source: Consistent with previous reports, glutamine carbon contributes to all TCA cycle intermediates and was significantly enriched in several amino acids (e.g. glutamate, aspartate, alanine, and proline) found to be reduced in Slc1a5 targeted cells (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Glutamine nitrogen was significantly enriched in glutamate, aspartate, alanine, serine, glycine and proline.
source: Similarly, glutamine nitrogen was significantly enriched in glutamate, aspartate, alanine, serine, glycine and proline (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Asparagine carbon was enriched only in aspartate, malate, fumarate, and citrate.
source: Consistent with the minor effects of asparagine withdrawal on markers of amino acid depletion, asparagine carbon was enriched only in aspartate, malate, fumarate, and citrate (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Asparagine nitrogen was enriched in aspartate, glutamate, proline, serine, and alanine.
source: On the other hand, asparagine nitrogen was enriched in aspartate, glutamate, proline, serine, and alanine (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Glutamine contributes both carbon and nitrogen for amino acid biosynthesis whereas asparagine carbon is used only for aspartate biosynthesis while asparagine nitrogen is used in transamination reactions.
source: Thus, glutamine contributes both carbon and nitrogen for amino acid biosynthesis whereas asparagine carbon is used only for aspartate biosynthesis while asparagine nitrogen is used in transamination reactions.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the isotope tracing data showing differential labeling patterns.

claim: The amino acids derived from either glutamine carbon (e.g. Glu, Ala, Asp, Pro) and nitrogen (e.g. Glu, Ala, Asp, Ser, Gly and Pro) and asparagine carbon (e.g. Asp) and nitrogen (e.g. Asp, Pro, Ala, Ser) were significantly enriched in total protein.
source: Importantly, the amino acids derived from either glutamine carbon (e.g. Glu, Ala, Asp, Pro) and nitrogen (e.g. Glu, Ala, Asp, Ser, Gly and Pro) and asparagine carbon (e.g. Asp) and nitrogen (e.g. Asp, Pro, Ala, Ser) were significantly enriched in total protein (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data in protein shown in Figure 6C-D.

claim: NEAA did not rescue proliferation but could rescue the induction of terminal osteoblast marker genes like Ibsp and to a lesser extent Bglap in Slc1a5-deficient cells.
source: Rescue experiments found NEAA did not rescue proliferation but could rescue the induction of terminal osteoblast marker genes like Ibsp and to a lesser extent Bglap in Slc1a5-deficient cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: Slc1a5 provides glutamine and asparagine that are used for de novo synthesis of many amino acids (e.g. Glu, Asp, Ala, Ser, Gly, and Pro) that can be incorporated into nascent protein in osteoblasts.
source: These data indicate Slc1a5 provides glutamine and asparagine that are used for de novo synthesis of many amino acids (e.g. Glu, Asp, Ala, Ser, Gly, and Pro) that can be incorporated into nascent protein in osteoblasts.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the isotope tracing data showing labeled amino acids in protein.

claim: GLS inhibition using BPTES resulted in cellular effects similar to Slc1a5 ablation.
source: GLS inhibition using BPTES resulted in cellular effects similar to Slc1a5 ablation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the subsequent data showing similar molecular and cellular changes with BPTES treatment.

claim: GLS inhibition significantly reduced glutamine carbon and nitrogen contribution to amino acid synthesis.
source: GLS inhibition using BPTES resulted in cellular effects similar to Slc1a5 ablation. GLS inhibition significantly reduced glutamine carbon and nitrogen contribution to amino acid synthesis and reduced the intracellular concentrations of glutamate, aspartate, alanine, serine, and glycine concentrations (Figure 6E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: GLS inhibition reduced the intracellular concentrations of glutamate, aspartate, alanine, serine, and glycine.
source: GLS inhibition using BPTES resulted in cellular effects similar to Slc1a5 ablation. GLS inhibition significantly reduced glutamine carbon and nitrogen contribution to amino acid synthesis and reduced the intracellular concentrations of glutamate, aspartate, alanine, serine, and glycine concentrations (Figure 6E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: GLS inhibition increased the presence of uncharged Glu, Asp, and Pro tRNA without affecting either Gln or Val tRNA charging.
source: Consistent with reduced amino acid concentrations, GLS inhibition increased the presence of uncharged Glu, Asp, and Pro tRNA without affecting either Gln or Val tRNA charging (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by tRNA charging assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: GLS inhibition induced eIF2α Ser51 phosphorylation and reduced S6 Ser240/244 phosphorylation.
source: Finally, GLS inhibition induced eIF2α Ser51 phosphorylation and reduced S6 Ser240/244 phosphorylation (Figure 6H).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6H.
